question: Which Nobel Laureate in Literature refused the prize in 1964, only for it to still be recorded in his name?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Jean-Paul Sartre**__.

**__Key Points__**

__

• **Jean-Paul Sartre**, a prominent figure in **20th-century French philosophy**, was awarded the **Nobel Prize in Literature** in **1964**.

• He was a leading proponent of **existentialism** and **Marxism**, exerting a significant influence on sociology, critical theory, and literary studies.

• Sartre became the first person to voluntarily decline the Nobel Prize, stating that a writer should not allow themselves to be transformed into an **institution**, even if it takes place in the most honorable form.

• He had previously declined other honors, including the **Legion of Honour** in **1945**, to maintain his **intellectual independence** and objective stance.

• Despite his public refusal and a letter sent to the **Swedish Academy** to withdraw his name, the committee announced him as the winner, and his name remains permanently recorded in the official list of **Nobel Laureates** for **1964**.

 **Additional Information__**

• **Gabriel Garcia Marquez**:

• A Colombian novelist and journalist who received the prize in **1982**.

• He is best known for his masterpiece **One Hundred Years of Solitude** and for popularizing the literary style known as **magical realism**.

• **Bob Dylan**:

• An American singer-songwriter who was awarded the Nobel Prize in **2016**.

• He was recognized for creating new poetic expressions within the great **American song tradition**, becoming the first musician to receive the honor.

• **Samuel Beckett**:

• An Irish avant-garde novelist and playwright who won the award in **1969**.

• A key figure in the **Theatre of the Absurd**, his most famous work is the play **Waiting for Godot**.
